### 📓 Docs Drift Check
**2** anchor(s) derived from **1** changed package(s); no hand-written page names any of them. ⚠️ **2** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/spec/liveness/action.json`, `packages/spec/liveness/state-counts/action.md`), so the pages documenting them are **NOT COVERED by this run** — this is not a clean bill of health for those files.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **2** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/spec/liveness/action.json`, `packages/spec/liveness/state-counts/action.md`) — pages documenting those are invisible to this run
- the SDK route bridge reached **55** of **207** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **152** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **152**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **97** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **147** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 96e7a4335c0aa611a706664da6df339f672ec1ab` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `cebef39ca4aff172805243a49ba19be7fb37d7c7` — the merge of head `4b5b87d21cb159072eabbd32bc58fc27c1827d6d` into base `96e7a4335c0aa611a706664da6df339f672ec1ab`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin cebef39ca4aff172805243a49ba19be7fb37d7c7 && git checkout cebef39ca4aff172805243a49ba19be7fb37d7c7
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 96e7a4335c0aa611a706664da6df339f672ec1ab 4b5b87d21cb159072eabbd32bc58fc27c1827d6d && git checkout -B drift-repro 96e7a4335c0aa611a706664da6df339f672ec1ab && git merge --no-ff 4b5b87d21cb159072eabbd32bc58fc27c1827d6d

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 96e7a4335c0aa611a706664da6df339f672ec1ab
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `d96cc5bbb6cc9d0a35d2c1a4914b9d836a8b4699`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/spec/src/system/translation.zod.ts, packages/spec/src/ui/action.zod.ts + packages/spec/liveness/action.json, packages/spec/liveness/state-counts/action.md, packages/lint/src/lint-liveness-properties.test.ts, packages/spec/liveness/object.json (`externalSharingModel`, the control row), packages/spec/scripts/liveness/check-liveness.mts (`authorWarnOnLive`, `EVIDENCE_SCANNED_STATUSES`, `evidenceScope`), content/docs/protocol/objectui/actions.mdx, the four regenerated content/docs/references/** pages, .changeset/26619-console-disabled-reason.md, ui/packages/components/src/renderers/layout/containers.tsx (`headerActions`, `buttonable`, `disabledReasonFor`, inline and overflow), ui/packages/plugin-detail/src/renderers/record-quick-actions.tsx (`actions` memo, `QuickActionButton`), ui/packages/app-shell/src/views/DeclaredActionsBar.tsx (`DeclaredActionButton`, button and `asMenuItem`), ui/packages/components/src/renderers/action/disabled-reason.tsx (`useDisabledReason`, `DisabledReasonTrigger`, `DisabledReasonMenuLabel`) and the four `action:*` renderers, ui/packages/react/src/hooks/useActionTextLocalizer.ts, ui/packages/i18n/src/useObjectLabel.ts (`actionSuffixes`, `resolve`, `actionDisabledReason`), ui/packages/i18n/src/pickLocalized.ts, ui/packages/types/src/ui-action.ts, ui/packages/core/src/actions/__tests__/actionKeys.pin.test.ts (main's own red), the five new test suites and the moved identity pin

Ruling executed: 6442737825 on #26619, letter A, second half (the console readers). Inputs read: the card body and all seven comments (triage 6440296436, brief 6441887048, ruling 6442737825, claim 6444476085, os-dev-report 6446453447 for PR 1, landing note 6449918956, os-dev-report 6451252645 for this PR); PR #26786's two contract records (6446707981, 6447429917) and its ACCEPT (6448592048) as background for what this PR owes; the PR #26869 body, its 28-file list, the net diff `origin/main...pr26869` (merge-base `aeb9cf0dd`, 28 files, +824/-60, matching the file list exactly); and the check-runs on `d96cc5bbb` at 19:15Z and 19:19Z.

**Head provenance.** `d96cc5bbb` is two commits on a branch restarted from `main` at `aeb9cf0dd`, which carries the #26786 merge `13dc413f` as an ancestor, so the spec half this PR reads is the merged one. `f6a479a30` is the feature; `d96cc5bbb` moves the `useObjectLabel` identity pin 27 to 28. `origin/main` is at `8eef9a8db`, three commits past the branch point, none touching a PR path.

**Check-runs on the head at review time (19:19:28Z, two REST reads):** 58 runs, 19 `success`, 5 `skipped`, 34 `in_progress`, 0 `failure`. Rendered and green: `Spec property liveness` (the `check:liveness` gate that reads the flipped row), `Lint · docs & code guards` (the `check:doc-authoring` Rule 3 walk over the describe strings), `Lint · ESLint`, `Lint · PM dispatch-gates`, `Lint · repo & tooling gates`, `Lint · CI, release & engine gates`, `Check Changeset`, `Governed Surface Queue Guard`, `PR-body guards`, `Build UI Deps`, `Check Documentation Links`, `Flag docs affected by code changes`, `Plan Test Core shards`, `Dogfood Regression Gate`. Still running: `Test Core` 1 to 8 (the lint silence pin and the spec suites live there), `Test UI` 1 to 16 (the five new suites and the identity pin), `Type Check UI`, `Type Check` x4, `Build Core`, `Build Docs`, `Build & E2E UI`, `Lint UI`, `Lint · scoped · tooling self-tests`. One `Test UI` shard is expected to go red on `ui/packages/core/src/actions/__tests__/actionKeys.pin.test.ts` ("missing: disabledReason"): that pin reds on `main` itself since #26786 landed, the fix is the seat's #26859, which is still OPEN at review time, and this PR does not touch `actionKeys.ts`. It is main's red, not this PR's, and is not counted here; see ③ for what the queue needs. This record judges the tree; the queue guard holds the PR until every check is green.

### ① Derived judgments

**What PR 1 promised this PR would do, judged one by one.**

1. **Liveness row `disabledReason` flipped to `live` with real readers as evidence: RIGHT.** `packages/spec/liveness/action.json` now reads `status: live`, `verifiedAt: 2026-10-27`, `evidenceScope: in-repo`, and an `evidence` string naming seven pointers. Each was read in the diff and resolves to a hunk that reads the key: `containers.tsx#disabledReasonFor`, `record-quick-actions.tsx#QuickActionButton`, `DeclaredActionsBar.tsx#DeclaredActionButton`, `disabled-reason.tsx#useDisabledReason`, `useActionTextLocalizer.ts#useActionTextLocalizer`, `useObjectLabel.ts#useObjectLabel` (`actionDisabledReason`), plus the two framework pointers carried over from the planned row (`i18n-resolver.ts#translateAction`, `i18n-extract.ts#collectExpectedEntries`). `evidenceScope: in-repo` is the gate's optional scope marker (`check-liveness.mts`, the EVIDENCE SCOPE block): it records that the look was this repo alone, which is the truth for a console reader that lives under `ui/`. `live` is in `EVIDENCE_SCANNED_STATUSES`, so the gate resolves every pointer, and `Spec property liveness` is green on this head. `liveness/state-counts/action.md` was regenerated: live 47 to 48, planned 1 to 0, classified 49 unchanged.
2. **`authorWarn` and `authorHint` dropped: RIGHT, and required.** `check-liveness.mts#scanAuthorWarnRows` pushes a `live` row carrying `authorWarn` onto `report.authorWarnOnLive`, which is a red condition. The row carries neither key. The `note` keeps the card id and the gate's own number; a `note` is maintainer prose the author-side lint never shows, so no tracker id reaches an author.
3. **Lint block turned into a silence pin, non-vacuous: RIGHT.** `lint-liveness-properties.test.ts` replaces the two warning-era cases with one. It authors `disabledReason` on an action AND `externalSharingModel: 'read'` on an object in the SAME `lintLivenessProperties` call; `externalSharingModel` is a `dead` row in the shipped `liveness/object.json` (read: `status: dead`, tombstoned under ADR-0049), so the call must draw `LIVENESS_DEAD_PROPERTY` for it, and does, while `ruleOf(findings, 'disabledReason')` is `undefined`. A lint that stopped loading ledgers would answer `[]` for both and fail the first assertion, which is what makes the silence a reading. The block then reads the shipped `action.json` row through the file's existing `shippedLedgerDir()` helper and pins `status === 'live'`, no `authorWarn`, no `authorHint`, and that `evidence` contains `containers.tsx#disabledReasonFor`. The precedent (`outcomeMessages`) was followed. The test is in `@objectstack/lint`, so its verdict is `Test Core`'s, still running.
4. **`.describe()` texts and `actions.mdx` back in the present tense, no tracker id in a describe string: RIGHT.** `action.zod.ts` line 1586 and `translation.zod.ts` line 218 now say what the console does ("Display-only reason a greyed action shows (its hover title and accessible description, or a menu item's second line) while `disabled` evaluates TRUE"; "Translated reason a greyed action shows (hover title and accessible description) while its `disabled` predicate is TRUE"). A grep for a `#` followed by three to five digits over both strings returns zero; the card id stays in the adjacent `//` comment and docblock, where Rule 3 permits it. `content/docs/protocol/objectui/actions.mdx` line 339 drops "The console does not show it yet" and the `os validate` warning sentence for "The console shows it while the predicate is true, as the button's hover title and its accessible description (a menu item shows it under its label). Without it the reason is the console's default". The four regenerated reference pages carry the new strings byte for byte: `ui/action.mdx`, `data/object.mdx`, `kernel/metadata-plugin.mdx` the action text, `system/translation.mdx` the translation text at all five addresses. `Lint · docs & code guards` is green on this head.

**The readers, each one asked whether it renders the declared reason.**

5. **`containers.tsx#disabledReasonFor` (record header, inline and overflow): RENDERS IT.** The function reads `action.disabledReason` as a string, trims, and falls back to `tt('actions.notAvailableForRecord', 'Not available for this record')`. It is called from `renderButton` (inline) and from the `overflowActions.map` (the ⋯ menu). Both lists derive from `headerActions` (`buttonable = headerActions.filter(...)`, `ranked` from `buttonable`, `inlineActions` and `overflowActions` from `ranked`), and `headerActions` is the memo that runs every raw action through `localizeActionTexts(ctx?.objectName, a, ...)`. So the string `disabledReasonFor` reads is already the bundle's sentence, else the authored `I18nLabel` collapsed to the active language, which is why a plain `typeof === 'string'` check is sound there. Inline: the pre-existing objectui#11811 wrapper (Tooltip on the focusable span, `aria-describedby` on button and span to an `sr-only` copy). Overflow: `DropdownMenuItem` with `aria-labelledby` to the label span and `aria-describedby` to a visible second line. Default fallback: the generic key. Bundle translation: through the memo. Tested in `page-header-disabledReason-26619.test.tsx` (inline tooltip and description, overflow second line visible and as description, zh bundle outranking the authored English with the English asserted absent, default, predicate-false control asserting no `aria-describedby` and no declared text).
6. **`record-quick-actions.tsx#QuickActionButton` (record section bar): RENDERS IT.** The `actions` array is built by `localizeActionTexts(objectName || undefined, a, ...)` before any button renders; `QuickActionButton` reads `action.disabledReason` as a string, trims, falls back to the generic key, and the existing wrapper serves tooltip plus `sr-only` description. Tested in `record-quick-actions.disabledReason-26619.test.tsx` (declared string as description and tooltip, zh bundle outranking, default, control).
7. **`DeclaredActionsBar.tsx#DeclaredActionButton` (declared actions bar, button and override menu item): RENDERS IT.** `localizedTexts = localizeActionTexts(objectName, action)` is now resolved once and both `declaredLabel` and `declaredReason` come off it, so the reason and the label can never come from different bundle reads (the objectui#4265 discipline). `disabledReason` is the trimmed declared string when the DECLARED predicate holds, else the generic key, else `undefined`. The `asMenuItem` branch shows it as the visible second line with `aria-labelledby` and `aria-describedby`; the button branch wraps in the tooltip trigger with the `sr-only` copy. Tested in `DeclaredActionsBar.disabledReason-26619.test.tsx` (declared string as description and tooltip, accessible name stays `Archive`, zh bundle outranking, default, control).
8. **`disabled-reason.tsx#useDisabledReason` (the four `action:*` renderers): RENDERS IT, inline map honoured, bundle not consulted, and that is consistent with `label` on the same components.** The hook gains `declaredReason?: unknown`, collapses it with `pickLocalized(declaredReason, language)` (exact tag, base, regional twin, `default`, `en`, first value; own string properties only), trims, and falls back to the generic key. `action-button.tsx`, `action-icon.tsx`, `action-group.tsx` (both the inline member and the dropdown item) and `action-menu.tsx` pass `schema.disabledReason` or `action.disabledReason`. Rendering is the existing `DisabledReasonTrigger` (tooltip plus `sr-only` description, `describedByWithReason` keeping an authored `aria-describedby`) and `DisabledReasonMenuLabel` with `menuItemReasonAria` (second line, `aria-labelledby` and `aria-describedby`). Weighed against `label`: these four render `{schema.label}`, `{action.label}` and `{action.label || action.name}` verbatim, with no `useObjectLabel` and no `pickLocalized` on the label at all. The reason therefore gets one step MORE localisation than the label on the same component (a map collapses instead of rendering as an object), and no less bundle treatment. A bundle lookup there would need a key object the SDUI node does not carry, as the dev says; a registered action reaches these renderers through a localising surface already carrying the bundle's sentence. Consistent, documented in the module header, and the dev's out-of-scope note is answered. Tested in `action-disabled-reason-26619.test.tsx`, three button sites by five cases and two menu sites by three cases: declared string as description AND tooltip with the default asserted absent from the tooltip, `{ en, 'zh-CN' }` map collapsed to the zh sentence under a zh provider, default in en and in zh (`对此记录不可用`), `{ en: '  ' }` falling back to the default, predicate-false control; menu: declared second line visible and as description with the accessible name staying `Archive`, default, control.
9. **Translation through the bundle (`useObjectLabel.actionDisabledReason` and `useActionTextLocalizer`): RIGHT.** `actionDisabledReason(objectName, actionName, fallback?)` is the `actionConfirm` pattern verbatim: `resolve(actionSuffixes(objectName, actionName, 'disabledReason'), fallback ?? '')` then `resolved || undefined`. `actionSuffixes` yields `objects.{o}._actions.{a}.disabledReason` (with the namespace-stripped twin) for a bound action and `globalActions.{a}.disabledReason` for an object-less one, the same two addresses `translateAction` and `os i18n extract` use. In the localizer the reason is collapsed with `pickLocalized` whenever declared (`!== undefined`), returned collapsed on the nameless path, and on the named path replaced by `actionDisabledReason(keyObject, name, collapsed.disabledReason)`. Declared-only holds: an action with no key never has `disabledReason` added, even when the bundle holds an entry (pinned). Blank handling: a map whose active-language value is `''` collapses to `''`, the resolver answers `undefined`, every reader's `typeof === 'string'` check misses and the default shows; a whitespace value passes through as whitespace and every reader's `trim() !== ''` catches it. The acceptance note "a blank reason falls back to the default on every surface" is true in the tree. `useObjectLabel` has one return path (the memo holds with or without a provider; `SAFE_FIELD_LABEL_FALLBACK` is reached only by `useSafeFieldLabel`, which the localizer does not use), so the new member is present wherever the localizer destructures it. Tested in `useActionTextLocalizer.disabledReason-26619.test.tsx` (6): authored string, bundle outranks authored at the object address, map collapsed to zh, `globalActions` address, no key added when undeclared, nameless map collapsed.
10. **`UIActionSchema.disabledReason` truly derived from the spec: RIGHT.** `ui/packages/types/src/ui-action.ts` declares `disabledReason?: SpecAction['disabledReason']` where `SpecAction` is `Action` imported from `@objectstack/spec/ui` (`@objectstack/spec: workspace:^`), beside `disabled?: SpecAction['disabled']`. The type is the spec's `I18nLabel` union by reference, not a re-spelling.
11. **Hover title and accessible description both served, as the card asked: YES.** On every button surface the reason is served twice: as a tooltip that opens on hover and on keyboard focus of the wrapper span (a native `title` cannot open on a natively disabled button, which the objectui#11811 and #11839 mechanics ruled and documented), and as a persistent `aria-describedby` to an `sr-only` copy that a screen reader hears with the tooltip closed. On a menu item the reason is a visible second line that is the item's description while the name stays the label, because a disabled item is unreachable by hover and by roving focus. The new suites assert both channels per site (`findByRole('tooltip')` after `user.hover`, and `aria-describedby` resolving to the declared text).
12. **Tests non-vacuous: YES.** Every suite has a declared-reason case asserting text (`Finish the checklist before archiving.`) the pre-change readers could never produce, a default case, and a predicate-false control that asserts the absence of `aria-describedby` and of the declared text; the bundle cases assert the zh sentence present and the authored English absent. The identity pin `useObjectLabel-identity-5564` moves 27 to 28 with the ledger comment naming `actionDisabledReason`, which is one new member and the honest arithmetic. The `-11811` and `-11839` sibling suites are byte-identical to `main` and still pin the generic text for actions that declare none, so they remain a control. One nit: the `action:*` case titled "a map with no usable entry for the language falls back to the default" authors `{ en: '  ' }` under an en provider, which is a BLANK entry for the language, not a missing one (a map with no entry at all for the language would fall through `pickLocalized`'s `en` and first-value limbs and show whatever it finds). The assertion is real; the title overstates it. Should-fix, the dev's call.
13. **Accept-set and public-surface changes the diff implies.** Spec accept-set: none; `actionDisabledReason()` and `actionTranslationSchema` are untouched, only their `.describe()` strings move. Public surface in `@object-ui/*`: `UIActionSchema.disabledReason` (new optional member, `@object-ui/types`); `useObjectLabel()` gains `actionDisabledReason` (`@object-ui/i18n`); `useActionTextLocalizer` now emits `disabledReason` on its returned copy when declared (`@object-ui/react`). `useDisabledReason`'s second parameter is module-private: nothing in `renderers/action/` is re-exported from the components entry (header says so; the entry files carry no reference). All additive. Judged under ② for the level.

### ② Semver level

Changeset `.changeset/26619-console-disabled-reason.md` at the ROOT `.changeset/`: `@objectstack/spec`, `@object-ui/types`, `@object-ui/i18n`, `@object-ui/react`, `@object-ui/components`, `@object-ui/plugin-detail`, `@object-ui/app-shell`, all `patch`; `Clause-②: no`; `Metadata-protocol: none`. The PR body carries the same two lines.

- **Root placement: RIGHT.** `ui/AGENTS.md` (the changeset bullet) says changesets are written at the repo root and that `ui/.changeset/` holds only pre-merge leftovers the root config does not read; the root `.changeset/config.json` lists every one of the seven packages in its single `fixed` group, and `privatePackages.version: true` covers `@object-ui/app-shell` (`private: true`). `Check Changeset` is green.
- **`Clause-②: no`: RIGHT.** No published schema's accept set moves; the spec diff is two describe strings, the ledger row and its state count.
- **`Metadata-protocol: none`: RIGHT.** Nothing an author can write changes. The key, its shape, its blank refusal and its translation slot were `added` by #26786; this PR makes the console honour them. A reader catching up to a declared contract is not a changed meaning or default of the key.
- **`patch`: RIGHT under the repo's rule, with the conventional reading named for the seat.** AGENTS.md Post-Task step 3 binds the level to the kind alone: a kind takes at least `minor`, `none` takes `patch`, and "a non-protocol change, widening or breaking, ships `patch`". Under plain semver the additions in ①.13 (a new member on an exported hook's return, a new optional field on an exported interface, a new key on a localizer's output) are a feature and would read `minor`. The repo rule is explicit and the seven packages sit in one `fixed` group with every `@objectstack/*` package, so the group's next number is the only thing the word decides. Not a must-fix; the seat may lift it to `minor` if it wants the CHANGELOG to say feature, and nothing in the tree would need to move.
- **`@objectstack/lint` without a changeset: fine.** The diff moves one test file there and no source; `Check Changeset` agrees.
- **Body matches what the diff publishes: YES on substance; one stale count.** Every "What changes" sentence was re-read against the tree and holds: the four surfaces, the two bundle addresses, the declared-only rule, the inline-map rule on the `action:*` renderers, the `UIActionSchema` derivation, the ledger flip with `evidenceScope: in-repo`, the dropped `authorWarn`/`authorHint`, the regenerated state count, the silence pin reading the shipped row, the two describe texts, the four regenerated reference pages, and the test inventory (6; 3x5 plus 2x3; 5; 4; 4). The stale sentence is a count that moved with the second commit: in "Test readings" the line `eslint over the 16 changed ui files: 0 errors (warnings are pre-existing \`no-explicit-any\`).` and in Human Minimum 3 the line `No formatter ran; eslint over the 16 changed ui files: 0 errors.` At `d96cc5bbb` the diff touches 17 files under `ui/` (the `useObjectLabel-identity-5564` pin joined in the second commit). Replacement for both: `eslint over the 17 changed ui files: 0 errors` with the rest of each sentence unchanged. `Lint · ESLint` is green on the head, so the claim is true in substance; only the number is stale. Should-fix.

### ③ Boundary flags

- **`open_questions`: `[]`** in the os-dev-report 6451252645. Nothing to answer.
- **Dev flag (out_of_scope_findings and acceptance note): the `action:*` renderers honour the inline map, not the bundle.** Answered in ①.8: consistent with how `label` is rendered on the same components, documented in the module header, and a bundle lookup there would need a key object the SDUI node does not carry. Not escalated; carrier stays `none`.
- **Dev flag (acceptance note): a blank reason falls back to the default on every surface, including a whitespace map value.** Verified in ①.9 for the localising surfaces and in ①.8 for the `action:*` renderers; pinned by the `{ en: '  ' }` case. Answered.
- **Main's own red, and what the queue needs.** `ui/packages/core/src/actions/__tests__/actionKeys.pin.test.ts` reds on `main` since #26786 ("missing: disabledReason" against `SPEC_ACTION_KEYS`). The fix is #26859 (`fix(ui): the action key inventory lists disabledReason`, two files: `actionKeys.ts` plus its changeset), OPEN and unmerged at 19:19Z. This PR does not add the row, correctly: the inventory is one file with one owner. Not counted against this head. Escalated to the seat as a sequencing fact: the merge queue's combined tree is green only once #26859 is in `main` ahead of this PR, or this branch merges `main` after it lands. The PR body's sentence "this branch takes it by a `main` merge once it lands" is a plan that is still true and still pending.
- **Skills-docs line.** The PR body says `Skills-docs: #26790`, which is the open card "skills(objectstack-ui, objectstack-i18n): the actions rule and the i18n skill do not teach an action's disabledReason (follow-up owed by #26619)". The card's landing note 6449918956 says "The skills row is #26820", which is a different card (the `books` translation group, owed by #26690). The PR is right and the landing note's number is a slip; a seat-side correction on the card, not a change to this PR.
- **Check-runs not yet rendered at review time.** `Test Core` 1 to 8, `Test UI` 1 to 16, `Type Check UI`, `Type Check` x4, `Build Core`, `Build Docs`, `Build & E2E UI`, `Lint UI`, `Lint · scoped · tooling self-tests`. The silence pin, the spec suites, the five new UI suites, the identity pin and the UI type-check are theirs to decide; the queue guard holds until they are green, the one `actionKeys` red excepted as above.
- **`premise_still_valid: true`** holds: at the branch point the console's `disabledReasonFor` returned only the generic sentence and the ledger row was `planned` with `authorWarn`; this head is the first tree where that is no longer so.
